exposure: crystalloid preloading (20 ml/kg Ringer's lactate before anesthesia)
crystalloid co-loading (20 ml/kg Ringer's lactate immediately after spinal administration)
cohort: The study included 160 parturients (ASA I-II) undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia.
finding: Coloading with crystalloids offered superior hemodynamic stability (higher systolic and diastolic blood pressure values) and a lower incidence of hypotension compared to preloading during spinal anesthesia for cesarean delivery, with comparable neonatal APGAR scores between groups.
